reviewer: Codex model review; no independent educator rater

excluded_sets.ela: No ELA text, reading, writing, or language standard is an intended score construct.
excluded_sets.science: No science instruction or NGSS alignment is claimed.
excluded_sets.humanities: No historical or humanities source interpretation is assigned.
excluded_sets.rehearsal: No teacher rehearsal, role-play, or simulated teacher dialogue is included; possible response patterns are diagnostic hypotheses, not a rehearsal.

ratings.title: Target and evidence agree
ratings.pass_when: The task elicits the stated learning target and claimed standard; any alignment limit is explicit.
ratings.reason: The stated target requires distinguishing area from perimeter, but students only answer an area question and a generic explanation; there is no direct perimeter or comparison prompt. The key rewards the opposite construct. The corrected version must elicit both quantities and meanings.

ratings.title: Content and keys are accurate
ratings.pass_when: Worked examples, accepted answers, units and scoring directions are correct and internally consistent.
ratings.locator: check-to-review.md:L3, L5; item 1 and teacher key
ratings.reason: Independent recomputation gives area 3 × 5 = 15 square units (B); 3 + 5 + 3 + 5 = 16 is perimeter in units. The key C and its square-unit label are wrong.

ratings.title: Claims and sources are represented honestly
ratings.pass_when: External claims have supporting opened sources; authored tasks and uncertain observations are labeled.
ratings.locator: check-to-review.md:L5; diagnosed disability and 80% mastery statements
ratings.reason: The artifact asserts a diagnosed disability from one distractor and universal mastery from a class percentage, with no supporting diagnostic, student, or source evidence. These are presented as facts, not tentative hypotheses. No factual diagnosis may be inferred from this artifact.

ratings.title: Materials are usable
ratings.pass_when: The promised student tasks, source stimuli, teacher directions and timing are present and feasible.
ratings.reason: The two short prompts are present, but no administration timing is supplied. There is no usable response-based reteaching/recheck task, and the written-only scoring direction conflicts with a mode-flexible explanation. Missing content is a failure of the supplied packet, not a reason to exclude the criterion.

ratings.title: Evidence supports the inference
ratings.pass_when: Individual learning, group products, behavior, simulation and missing evidence are distinguished; score claims stay within the data.
ratings.locator: check-to-review.md:L5; 80% class rule and omit-unanswered rule
ratings.reason: A class percentage cannot establish each learner's knowledge, a single choice cannot establish broad mastery, and dropping unanswered papers conceals missing evidence. The answer considered evidence of mastery is also incorrect.

ratings.title: Participation and support are appropriate
ratings.pass_when: Required supports, privacy and developmentally appropriate directions are preserved; no unjustified exclusion or harmful labeling.
ratings.reason: The blanket written-only rule introduces handwriting/oral-response demands beyond the math target and can exclude documented access supports; no supports exception is preserved. A single answer is used for harmful labeling and automatic placement.

ratings.title: Mathematical meaning
ratings.pass_when: Representations, symbols and operations agree; explanation matches the mathematical construct.
ratings.reason: The teacher explanation adds all side lengths and calls the result area in square units. Its operation and units do not match the intended mathematical quantity.

ratings.title: Student reasoning
ratings.pass_when: Tasks require the reasoning warranted by the target and accept defensible strategies.
ratings.reason: Drawing/description is a useful opening for reasoning, but the wrong key, restriction on oral assistance, and absent accepted-strategy criteria prevent defensible reasoning about interior square coverage and boundary length from being credited consistently.

ratings.title: Construct-preserving access
ratings.pass_when: Supports address a stated barrier and preserve required accommodations; changed constructs are disclosed.
ratings.reason: The policy bars oral assistance without distinguishing direction reading, scribing, a student's own oral explanation, and answer-giving hints. It does not preserve required accommodations or disclose how support affects the construct.

ratings.title: Usable language support
ratings.pass_when: Language objectives and actual models/frames fit the content; fading applies to optional prompts, not required access.
ratings.reason: No designated language-development objective or language scaffold is claimed, and no learner language profile requires a particular model/frame. This optional language-support criterion is inapplicable to the original; the broader oral-access problem is rated under A1 and C6.

ratings.title: Diagnostic interpretation
ratings.pass_when: Distractors and response patterns support tentative hypotheses; missing/ambiguous responses receive follow-up rather than unsupported labels.
ratings.locator: check-to-review.md:L5; distractor A diagnosis and missing-paper instruction
ratings.reason: The same answer can have multiple causes, but A is assigned a disability label without checking strategy. Blank and ambiguous responses receive no access check or follow-up.

ratings.title: Actionable follow-up
ratings.pass_when: The packet supplies a next teaching move and another task keyed to the observed evidence.
ratings.reason: Moving to volume is not tied to actual response evidence and no second task checks whether area/perimeter confusion is resolved. The word volume is ambiguous, so it is not rejected merely as a supposedly impossible grade 3 topic.

ratings.title: Need and intensity
ratings.pass_when: Activities match a documented target gap; tier, placement and cause are not inferred from a single score.
ratings.reason: A single distractor response is used to declare both cause and required support intensity; there is no documented target-gap history, corroboration, or team decision.

ratings.title: Implementation and monitoring
ratings.pass_when: The adult has models, keys, bounded scaffold decisions and feasible checks/regrouping rules.
ratings.locator: check-to-review.md:L5–L6; placement rule and next step
ratings.reason: Despite directing Tier 3 placement, the resource has no accurate intervention model, bounded scaffold decisions, monitoring check, or regrouping plan.

ratings.title: Policy and arithmetic
ratings.pass_when: Calculation uses the declared policy, correctly handles missing/exempt evidence and can be reproduced.
ratings.locator: check-to-review.md:L5; key, full-credit rule, 80% rule, missing-paper instruction
ratings.reason: Credit rests on an incorrect key and a response-mode restriction unrelated to the target. There is no reproducible scoring rule for the explanation or an explicit denominator; omitting unanswered papers obscures coverage.

ratings.title: Defensible interpretation
ratings.pass_when: Rollups retain coverage/support conditions; ordinal scales, growth and uncertainty are not misrepresented.
ratings.reason: The class rollup is substituted for individual evidence, support conditions are disregarded, and missing responses are erased. The interpretation exceeds what this brief task can establish.

limit: Summarizes supplied reviewer judgments only; no claim of classroom efficacy, psychometric validity or independent automated pedagogical evaluation.
